cell.label: START Initial clinical findings suggestive of CAP in age >1 month
Assess clinical signs and symptoms: - Respiratory rate for age above threshold - Fever >38ºC - O2 saturation less than 94% - Nasal flaring - Abnormal breath sounds - Increased work of breathing.
Measure respiratory rate (RR) by observation for 60 seconds when the child is awake and not crying. Tachypnea is: 1 to 12 months old: RR >50 1 to 5 years old: RR > 40 > 5 years old: RR >20.
Pneumonia not suspected, manage as appropriate.
Suspect viral infection. Consider diagnosis and treatment of influenza. Supportive treatment, no antibiotics needed. Monitor closely for possible bacterial/missed pneumonia.
Ambiguous clinical findings or age younger than 5 years with high fever of uncertain source.
Complication suspected or prolonged course unresponsive to antibiotics.
Consider: CXR, procalcitonin and WBC with differential.
Suspect viral pneumonia. Consider treatment of influenza in appropriate seasons. Supportive treatment, no antibiotics needed. Monitor closely for possible bacterial/ missed pneumonia.
Manage for specific complication. Consider infectious disease and/or pulmonology consult.
Follow up as appropriate. Adjust antibiotic, if necessary.
